camps.name: Boston Basin upper (high) camp
camps.why: The highest hardened camp in the basin, with a toilet. Sleeping here cuts several hundred feet off the pre-dawn approach to the climb.

camps.name: Boston Basin lower camp
camps.why: First hardened camp up the trail, with a toilet and trees; it melts out earlier but adds about a thousand feet to summit morning. Fall back here if the upper camp is full.

camps.name: Informal snow and rock bivouacs above the basins
camps.why: Unplanned shelter only, used by parties caught high or cut off by a failed glacier crossing. Not a place to plan a night.

camps.name: Informal snow and rock bivouacs above the basins
camps.why: The small perch at the toe of the North Ridge, reached after the Boston Glacier crossing. Sleeping here puts the rope on the ridge at first light; space is tiny and exposed.

plan_conflict: The bivouacs entry on file calls ridge bivies emergency-only, but this route's own plan sleeps night 2 on a ridge bivy, so it is promoted to main for night 2.

camps.name: Boston Basin high camp
camps.why: The standard base for the ridge: sleep here, climb the couloir and ridge the next day and come back to the tent. Permits for the basin are hard to get.

camps.name: Treeline emergency bivy
camps.why: Only for parties benighted on the walk in. There are no prepared sites, so do not plan a night here.

camps.name: Boston Basin upper (high) camp
camps.why: Benched sites in the upper basin under the Taboo Glacier. Night 1 after the hike in, night 2 after the summit day, with the hike out the next morning.

camps.name: Boston Basin lower camp
camps.why: First hardened camp up the trail, with a toilet and trees; it melts out earlier but adds about a thousand feet to summit morning. Fall back here if the upper camp is full.

camps.name: Informal snow and rock bivouacs above the basins
camps.why: Unplanned shelter only, used by parties caught high or cut off by a failed glacier crossing. Not a place to plan a night.

camps.name: Boston Basin high camp
camps.why: Staging camp for the traverse, about two hours from the base of Torment. It is crowded and permits are tight, but it makes a day-two start possible.

camps.name: Torment Basin camp below the southeast face
camps.why: Alternative when Boston Basin permits are gone: it starts the traverse at the foot of Torment, on snow early in the season, with a longer carry in.

camps.name: Mid-traverse ridge bivy
camps.why: A flat notch on the connecting ridge with a snow moat for melting water. Most parties bivy here after Torment, then finish Forbidden the next morning.

plan_conflict: On file the ridge bivy is called an emergency option, but reports and this plan make it the planned night-2 sleep, so it is promoted to main for night 2.

camps.name: Boston Basin high camp
camps.why: Upper camp with a toilet; the glacier starts near the tents so summit day is short. Night 2 follows the climb, before the hike out.

camps.name: Boston Basin low camp
camps.why: Sheltered moraine camp near trees that melts out earlier, at the cost of an extra thousand feet on summit morning. Use when the upper camp is still snowbound.

camps.name: Sahale Glacier Camp
camps.why: The only permitted camp up here, with rock-walled pads and a toilet at the foot of the glacier. It is very exposed to wind, but it puts the summit close for an early start.

camps.name: Doubtful Lake
camps.why: A sheltered, lower fallback about a mile and a thousand feet below the arm. Only worth it in bad weather or when the high camp has no space.

camps.name: Boston Basin upper (high) camp
camps.why: Standard base for the tower: about 6,200 ft, with a toilet and a shorter morning than sleeping low. Sharkfin is a short climb, so most parties then hike out.

camps.name: Boston Basin lower camp
camps.why: Lower, more sheltered camp near treeline that melts out sooner; costs about a thousand feet of extra climbing on summit morning.

camps.name: Informal snow and rock bivouacs above the basins
camps.why: Unplanned shelter only, used by parties caught high or cut off by a failed glacier crossing. Not a place to plan a night.

plan_conflict: The plan puts the night at a lower camp near 5,700 ft, but guidebook-style reports place the standard camp in the basin near 6,200 ft.

camps.name: Cascade-Johannesburg Col bivy
camps.why: Top of the CJ Couloir, on the plan's day-1 end point. It saves the long haul on summit day, but the couloir below is exposed to rockfall from Johannesburg.

camps.name: Johannesburg Camp
camps.why: A walk-in camp just above the Cascade Pass trailhead. Use it to be at the road end the night before, then climb the couloir on day 1.

camps.name: Basin camp below Colonial Glacier
camps.why: Tarn-side camp near 6,100 ft right under the glacier, so the summit day is short and water is close. It is a long steep first day.

camps.name: Colonial Basin bench camps, below the Pyramid-Colonial col
camps.why: Bench camps at about 5,400 to 5,900 ft are a shorter first day but have little water on the way, and they add an hour to summit morning.

plan_conflict: Both Colonial camps were marked main on file; the plan and reports put night 1 in the basin under the glacier, so the bench camps are changed to route.

camps.name: Cosho Camp, Fisher Creek
camps.why: Roomy forest camp on Fisher Creek with water at the door. Sleep here after the Easy Pass day and again after the summit day, before the climb back out.

camps.name: Eldorado-Inspiration snow arm high camp
camps.why: The usual base for the Dorado climbs, on snow or bare rock near the Eldorado east ridge. Sleep here before and after the summit day; the glacier crossing starts from camp.

camps.name: Roush Creek Basin camp
camps.why: Lower camp east of Eldorado Basin, useful when Eldorado Basin is full or for a shorter first day. Costs the height back on day 2.

camps.name: Marble Creek Campground, Cascade River Road
camps.why: A road campground for the night before, used when the permit has to be activated in person. It is not a night on the climb.

camps.name: Eldorado East Ridge rock bivies
camps.why: Flat rock at the toe of the east ridge, firmer than snow once the snowpack retreats. It is the same camp area as the high camp, just on rock.

camps.name: Eldorado Basin camp
camps.why: Lower vegetated camp with running water. Parties who start late or find the boulder field slow stop here and carry up the next morning.

camps.name: Klawatti Col camp
camps.why: Only for longer trips that link Klawatti or Austera with Dorado Needle. Reaching it means a roped crossing of the Inspiration Glacier.

plan_conflict: Roush Creek Basin camp and Marble Creek Campground were marked main on file; reports and the plan sleep nights 1 and 2 at the high camp, so those two are changed to route.
